entry.title: Let the dev question editor publish edits as a GitHub PR
entry.content:
Let the dev question editor publish edits as a GitHub PR

/dev/questions previously only let you edit questions in localStorage and
export a JSON blob for manual hand-porting. Add a publish-item-edits Edge
Function that takes those edits, merges them into
web/src/data/devOverrides.json, and opens a PR against the repo; loadItemBank
now merges that file on top of the hand-authored banks so a merged PR takes
effect for every visitor. The server re-checks the caller's email against an
allowlist before touching GitHub, since the client-side gate is only a UI
courtesy.

entry.title: Add a developer question-bank view for editing assessment items
entry.content:
Add a developer question-bank view for editing assessment items

Adds /dev/questions, gated to an email allowlist, that lists every
assessment item grouped by concept/topic and lets a developer edit an
item's difficulty, wording, format, status, and other fields, or author
a brand-new item. Since items are static TypeScript literals rather than
database rows, edits are kept as a local override layer (localStorage)
merged over the base bank for display, with an export button to hand off
the JSON for merging back into the source files.

entry.title: Render LaTeX math in assessment items, not just wiki lessons
entry.content:
Render LaTeX math in assessment items, not just wiki lessons

Item stems, MCQ choices, rubric element descriptions, and code-test
descriptions previously only supported inline code spans
(CodeText/splitCode), on the assumption that "assessment stems never
need maths." They do: probability/stats items are full of formulas.
CodeText now shares the wiki's $...$ math + `code` splitter
(lib/wiki/inlineMath.ts) and renders math spans with the same KaTeX
InlineMath component the wiki already uses, so authors can write
"$P(X>k) = (1-p)^k$" in an item and have it render properly wherever
item text is shown.

entry.title: Fix unsubmittable geometric-distribution factory-inspector item
entry.content:
Fix unsubmittable geometric-distribution factory-inspector item

The item asked two questions (expected count and a tail probability)
but used format "numeric" with a single free-text input. Its
answerKey ("E[X]=25; P(X>30)=0.96^30≈0.2939") isn't parseable as a
number, so gradeMath() threw on Number(item.answerKey) and the
question could never be submitted. Split it into two numeric items,
one per sub-question, each with a plain numeric answerKey.
